text: 支持“卖淫合法化”的本质是支持“嫖娼合法化”。
en: Supporting 'legalisation of prostitution' is essentially the same as supporting 'legalisation of patronising prostitutes'.

text: 民国发达地区明娼和暗娼的比例为1：2，平均每20个女性（不仅是成年妇女）就有1个妓女。
en: In the developed areas of the Republic of China era, the ratio of open prostitutes to clandestine prostitutes was 1:2; on average, one in every twenty females (not merely adult women) was a prostitute.

text: 可以说，无论做不做合法化，私下的买卖交易都不会减少。
en: One could say that, legalised or not, private buying-and-selling transactions will not decrease.

text: 荷兰开放性交易23年，目前的状态是犯罪组织把非法入境、人口贩卖、性交易做成了有机循环。
en: The Netherlands has had an open sex trade for 23 years, and the current situation is that criminal organisations have turned illegal entry, human trafficking and sex trading into an organic cycle.

text: 性交易者中，有三分之一是荷兰人，其余为东欧移民，其中三分之二左右受到过胁迫和威胁。
en: Among those in the sex trade, one third are Dutch, the rest being Eastern European immigrants, of whom around two thirds have been coerced and threatened.

text: 为什么被贩卖的非法移民为主呢，因为合法化以后妓女不挣钱了。
en: Why are trafficked illegal immigrants the main group? Because after legalisation prostitutes no longer make money.

text: 国内愿意做的人少，那只能从低收入国家拐人来干。
en: With few people at home willing to do it, they can only abduct people from low-income countries to do the work.

text: 阿姆斯特丹市长亲口承认，用红灯区解决强奸失败了。
en: The mayor of Amsterdam admitted personally that using the red-light district to combat rape has failed.

text: 不好使、没有用，短期内确实强奸率下降了，但是长期借此滋生的黑社会，产生的问题远比解决的多。
en: It does not work, it is of no use; in the short term the rape rate did fall, but in the long run the gangland it breeds gives rise to far more problems than it solves.

text: 看完觉得有的男性性方面真的有点可怜，没有性就会疯狂？
en: After reading this I felt that some men are really rather pathetic when it comes to sex—do they go mad without it?

text: 女人无法理解。
en: Women cannot understand.

text: 大部分女人一辈子没有性也不会太难受，被强迫性行为才会很难受。
en: Most women would not suffer too badly even going their whole lives without sex; it is only forced sex that causes real distress.

text: 我很同情也理解底层男想嫖娼的心态，爱情毕竟是奢侈品。
en: I sympathise with and understand the lower-class men who want to patronise prostitutes; love, after all, is a luxury.

text: 但是底层男性嫖娼的对象是底层妓女，而不是年入几十万的高级外围。
en: But the women lower-class men patronise are lower-class prostitutes, not high-end escorts earning hundreds of thousands a year.

text: 而底层妓女的生活，恐怕很难比底层男性好多少。
en: And the lives of lower-class prostitutes are probably little better than those of lower-class men.

text: 嘴上说着要公平，要求放开嫖娼去剥削更悲惨的人。
en: They talk of fairness, yet demand liberalising prostitution so as to exploit those even worse off.

text: 恐怕对不起那嘴上挂着的公平正义。
en: This hardly befits the fairness and justice they keep on their lips.

text: 我一直记得在知乎看过一个回答，东北下岗，下岗的老公拉着老婆去卖淫，孩子在学校被骂。
en: I have always remembered an answer I read on Zhihu: during the layoffs in the Northeast, a laid-off husband dragged his wife into prostitution, and the child was bullied at school.

text: 虽然她养活了全家，但是收获的不可能是感激，如果染病了，也只会被抛弃唾骂。
en: Although she supported the whole family, what she received could never be gratitude; if she contracted an illness, she would only be abandoned and reviled.

text: 有的人把卖淫和环卫工类比，说都是一样被嫌弃的工作，实在是可笑。
en: Some compare prostitution with street cleaners, saying both are equally looked-down-upon jobs—it is truly laughable.

text: 在他心里这个世界是什么样的呢？
en: What does the world look like in his mind?

text: ——更新分界线——
en: ——更新分界线——

text: 很多人拿妓女月入几十万还有高级外围来评论我，(눈_눈)？
en: Many people cite prostitutes earning hundreds of thousands a month and high-end escorts to criticise me, (눈_눈)?

text: 这是底层妓女吗？
en: Are these lower-class prostitutes?

text: 所以你们是连底层妓女都没听闻过吗？
en: So have you never even heard of lower-class prostitutes?

text: 就这还…
en: And with that...

text: 有人说我没有提包养，最反对包养的是原配吧？
en: Some say I didn't mention keeping a mistress; surely it is the legal wife who most opposes that?

text: 就反对包养这一点来说，男人女人是可以相互理解的。
en: On the point of opposing keeping a mistress, men and women can understand one another.

text: 有人说等女人四十就饥渴了，我是真不知道会不会。
en: Some say that once women turn forty they become desperate for sex; I genuinely don't know if that is true.

text: 三十如狼四十如虎，我三十了，没有感觉。
en: 'At thirty like a wolf, at forty like a tiger'—I am thirty and feel nothing.

text: 女人四十多要准备更年期绝经了…
en: Women in their forties are approaching menopause...

text: 但是瓢虫四十多，五十多，六十多还是会嫖。
en: But Ladybug, even in his forties, fifties and sixties, still patronises prostitutes.

text: 但是也有正常人不嫖娼，不支持卖淫合法化，我相信这种正常男人才是大多数。
en: But there are also normal men who do not patronise prostitutes and do not support legalising prostitution; I believe such normal men are the majority.

text: 而且也有纯爱的男性向漫画小说，也有不会放任自己的兽性的男人。
en: And there are also male-oriented manga and novels about pure love, and there are men who will not give in to their base urges.

text: 卖淫合法=削弱全体女性的价值=削弱全体女性的社会地位。
en: Legalising prostitution = diminishing the value of all women = lowering the social status of all women.

text: 这很好理解，一个纯粹的供需关系问题。
en: This is easy to understand: it is purely a matter of supply and demand.

text: 如果卖淫彻底消失，那么男性想满足客观存在且必然存在的性需求，就必须向女性寻求价值交换，在这一过程中，女性无形中提供了性价值作为筹码之一，并且这还是一种垄断资源；作为交换，男性必须付出同等价值的其他筹码，比如金钱，比如关照等等，这一关系才能“成交”。
en: If prostitution were to vanish entirely, then to satisfy their objectively existing and inevitably present sexual needs, men would have to seek an exchange of value from women; in this process women involuntarily offer their sexual value as one of the bargaining chips, and it is moreover a monopolised resource; in exchange, men must give up other chips of equal value—money, favour, and so on—for the transaction to be 'closed'.

text: 现在出现了卖淫行为，这彻底打破了原有的博弈平衡，被女性垄断的性资源变得不再稀缺，男性不再需要为性资源付出高昂的筹码，所以卖淫合法化=削弱了全体女性的社会地位。
en: Now that prostitution exists, it completely upends the original balance of the game: the sexual resources monopolised by women are no longer scarce, men need no longer pay a high price for them, and so legalising prostitution equals diminishing the social status of all women.

text: 所以，如果全体男性都是冷酷的绝对理性人（也就意味着不受礼法道德约束），那么全体男性都会支持卖淫合法的，即使他们中只会有很小一部分人会购买性服务，因为支持卖淫合法带来的好处，无论其自身是否真的购买性服务，都会惠及全体男性。
en: Therefore, if all men were cold, absolutely rational actors (meaning unconstrained by rites, laws and morals), then all men would support legalising prostitution, even though only a small fraction would actually buy sex, because the benefits of supporting legalisation accrue to all men regardless of whether they themselves ever purchase such services.

text: 所以这就不难理解为什么很多男性都会支持卖淫合法，这还真不意味着他们都想购买性服务。
en: Thus it is not hard to understand why many men support legalising prostitution; this certainly does not mean they all wish to buy sex.

text: 作为对立面，女性当然都会反对卖淫合法化，原因如前所述，卖淫合法化打破了自己的性资源垄断地位，进而削弱了自己的社会地位。
en: As the opposing side, women of course all oppose legalising prostitution; the reason, as stated above, is that legalisation breaks their monopolistic hold on sexual resources, and thereby diminishes their social standing.

text: 所以，综上所述，如果完全抛开礼法道德，那么是否支持卖淫合法化之争，本身就是全体男性和全体女性的社会博弈之争的一种表象，没什么值得特别关注的。
en: So, in summary, if one sets aside rites, laws and morality entirely, then the dispute over whether to support legalising prostitution is itself but a manifestation of the social contest between all men and all women—nothing especially worthy of attention.

text: 你以为合法化后的情景：每个月拿着微薄的工资，随便进出红灯区，想怎么爽就怎么爽，既不用担心被抓也不用担心伦理道德问题（毕竟满大街都是）
en: The scene you imagine after legalisation: with your meagre monthly wage, freely coming and going from the red-light district, enjoying yourself however you like, with no fear of arrest and no worry about ethics or morality (after all, it is everywhere on the streets).

text: 实际上合法化：各种人用各种手段，威逼利诱，拐卖，引诱吸毒等等控制你的姐妹，女儿，甚至是你的长辈，强迫卖淫。
en: The reality of legalisation: all manner of people, by every means—coercion, enticement, trafficking, luring into drugs, and so on—control your sisters, your daughters, even your elders, and force them into prostitution.

text: 你不得不攒着你的微薄的工资，希望哪天能赎回他们。
en: You are forced to save up your meagre wage, hoping to one day ransom them back.

text: 不要寄希望于法律，因为是合法的。
en: Do not pin your hopes on the law, for it is legal.

text: 你以为的黄就是你平时钻进小巷子里，满足你裤裆里的那点事。
en: The vice you imagine is merely you slipping into an alley to satisfy that urge in your trousers.

text: 实际上的黄，有整条利益链，涉及到黑道、白道、拐卖、毒品、贪腐、人生限制等等
en: The real vice involves an entire chain of interests, encompassing the underworld, the authorities, trafficking, drugs, corruption, deprivation of liberty, and more.

text: 记住，黄赌毒是一家的！
en: Remember, vice, gambling and drugs are all one family!

text: 反驳的大致分几点
en: The rebuttals fall roughly into a few categories.

text: 1.类比欧洲发达国家的。
en: 1. Those who draw analogies with developed European countries.

text: 南斯拉夫和乌克兰人民谢谢你们全家，别人不远万里跑过去做送温暖。
en: The people of Yugoslavia and Ukraine thank your whole family—others travel ten thousand miles to go and 'spread warmth'.

text: 2.逻辑类的。
en: 2. The logical ones.

text: 聊的是非自愿，聊的是合法化之后会让受胁迫的人员比例增加。
en: What is being discussed is the non-consensual aspect, and that after legalisation the proportion of coerced people will rise.

text: 如果产业链终端是白色的，就会给这堵法律围墙开个缺口。
en: If the end of the industry chain is 'white' (legitimate), it opens a breach in this wall of law.

text: 你今天认可正常死亡的象牙可以买卖，明天所有象牙都会来自正常死亡的象牙。
en: If today you accept that ivory from natural deaths may be traded, tomorrow all ivory will come from 'natural deaths'.

text: 3.以偏概全的，“合法化之前这些受胁迫的事本身就存在”“合法的时候，难道这些就不是被胁迫的”
en: 3. Those who take a part for the whole: 'these coerced cases already existed before legalisation' / 'once it is legalised, are these people suddenly not coerced?'

text: 合法的就是被胁迫，不合法的就是自己自愿的，这是这类想象的观点，不是发表的。
en: 'Legal means coerced, illegal means voluntary'—that is the view held by such people in their imagination, not what was actually argued.

text: 4.合法化后，也让这件事本身的道德阈值降低，不管是PC的还是卖的。
en: 4. After legalisation, the moral threshold of the act itself is lowered, both for those who buy (patronise) and those who sell.

text: 合法化下一步会不会是合理化，一旦走到这一步。
en: Will the step after legalisation be rationalisation, once things go that far?

text: 评论区那些着急的人，你希望你们的亲人、好友觉得这是一条正常的谋生道路吗？
en: Those of you in the comments who are so eager—do you wish for your loved ones and friends to see this as a normal means of making a living?

text: 更有人问我上班合法，你上班合法，也是被胁迫的？
en: Someone even asked me: going to work is legal, your job is legal—are you coerced too?

text: 看来普通社畜上班他们眼里已经可以和这件事同比了
en: It seems that in their eyes, ordinary wage slaves going to work can already be equated with this.

text: 刚开始很疑惑为什么会有这么多人用各种诡辩来反驳，后来想明白这群人只有私欲没有逻辑的。
en: At first I was puzzled why so many people used every kind of sophistry to argue back; later I realised this crowd has only selfish desire and no logic.

text: 一群极致而又愚蠢的利己主意者，以为条条框框的法律束缚住了自由。
en: A bunch of extreme and foolish egoists, who think the rigid strictures of law bind their freedom.

text: 以为突破这道看似不高的围墙，自己可以0成本干损人利己的事。
en: They think that by breaking through this seemingly low wall, they can harm others for their own gain at zero cost.

text: 以为礼义廉耻，公序良俗踩在脚底就可以自由的干鲜廉寡耻的事。
en: They think that by trampling rites, righteousness, honour and shame, public order and good customs underfoot, they can freely indulge in utterly shameless acts.

text: 殊不知是这堵围墙保护了底层的我们，保护我们不被掌握更多资源的人踩在脚底。
en: Little do they know that this wall protects us at the bottom, shielding us from being trampled underfoot by those who hold more resources.

text: 妄想着突然这道围墙成为猎杀者，殊不知突破这道围墙后等待着他们的是即使有法律束缚也早就是猎人的人。
en: They vainly dream that this wall suddenly becomes the predator, unaware that what awaits them beyond the wall are those who, even bound by law, were already hunters.

text: 和支持废除死刑的人一样，非蠢即坏！
en: Just like those who support abolishing the death penalty—they are either fools or knaves!
